body:
## Summary In edit mode, an admonition (a MyST `{note}`-style box) or a GitHub alert (`> [!NOTE]`) opened as one block: pressing Enter on a paragraph or list item reached with the arrows, or clicking one, opened the whole box. Now the element you select or point at is the one that opens; the whole box opens from its title or frame, or when it is itself selected. ## Deliverables | In edit mode, inside an admonition or alert | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Click a body paragraph or list item | the whole box opens | that paragraph or item opens | | Click the title or the frame | the whole box opens | the whole box opens | | Enter on an element reached with the arrows | the whole box opens | that element opens | | Enter on the box selected as a whole | the whole box opens | the whole box opens | | A diagram, formula or code directive of the body | the whole box opens | that directive opens as a whole, fences included | | Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Up/Down in the editor of a direct block of the body | no inner move | the block (for an item: its list) moves among the body's blocks, or the move is refused with a reason | | Down at the end of a list, Up at its start | the next block outside would open | the caret stays in the editor | | Erase an alert paragraph or item, then commit | an empty line cuts the alert | a `>` line keeps the alert whole | Text written on a directive's opening line is not a block of its own: the one-line body of `:::{warning} Text` or a card title opens the whole directive. Where the lines of an element cannot be told, the block or box around it opens (see Known gaps). ```mermaid flowchart LR render["render: mapBoxSourceLines
(mystBoxLines.ts)"] --> pick click[click or Enter] --> pick["editingElementFor
(mappedBlocks.ts)"] chord[move chord] --> moves["blockEditor.ts
blockMoves.ts"] moves -->|previewBlockMove| plan["planBlockMove
(quote prefix aware)"] commit[empty commit] --> drain["blockEdits.ts"] drain --> keep["planAlertPlaceholder
(sourceEdits.ts)"] ``` ## Changes - `editingElementFor` opens the whole admonition only when the box itself or its title is the target; a block of the body opens on its own lines, and a list around the box never takes it over. The nearest box decides when they are nested. - A new render pass, `mapBoxSourceLines`, runs inside admonitions, alerts, callouts and dropdowns: no block there maps part of a fence around it, or one fence line or HTML tag line of a pair without the other, and a diagram, formula, code, `{list-table}` or `{csv-table}` directive maps its whole directive. A block held directly by a list item keeps its own lines and takes only the empty lines under it; one the parser gives no position (the first paragraph of a tight item) reaches the next block of the item or its end. A formula whose own lines cannot be told is no block of its own, so the block or box around it opens. A `{div}` callout maps all of its lines, so its title opens the whole callout. The body of a version admonition maps the lines it is written on. In an admonition left open at the end of the file, a block inside it keeps its own closing fence (one quoted case is listed under Known gaps). Blocks outside a box are mapped as before. - The move chord works from the editor of a direct block of the body, never leaving the box; a refused move shows its reason next to the box's insert point. A block inside a list item, or in a quote, card or grid inside the box, does not move; nor does a `{table}` directive, with or without a caption, and no neighbouring block moves past it. A move that would put an unindented `---` line first in the body, or a heading first in an untitled admonition or in a callout, is refused, however the box is written (a callout class given by `:class:` or by a `---` block of options included): the content would not show, or the heading would become the title. - The move planner understands a GitHub alert's `>` prefix: a prefix-only line counts as blank and an added separator carries the prefix. - An erased block of an alert body is written as the alert's prefix alone. - A directive admonition holding an open editor no longer scrolls its own overflow, so the block palette does not cover the text box. - The keyboard navigation clip is re-filmed, down to an item of a nested sub-list; requirements, user guide and CHANGELOG follow. ## Impacts Users reach the elements of an admonition or alert directly, with the mouse or the keyboard. To edit the whole box with the mouse, click its title or its frame. In the editor of a GitHub alert block, the `> ` markers are part of the text. While an editor is open inside an admonition, wide content of that admonition does not scroll. The re-filmed keyboard navigation clip walks with the arrows into an admonition, down to an item of a nested sub-list, and Enter opens that line alone. It lasts 26.0 s with 15 key presses (MP4 0.52 MB, WebM 0.35 MB, GIF 1.62 MB at 960 px, 12 fps, 128 colours, the first step of the size ladder), filmed on Windows with VS Code 1.147.0 and the extension built from this change ([MP4](https://github.com/gsemet/markdown-okf-schema-studio/raw/f9dc2c630b852635e8bffcd0b00b42cc886b293c/docs/demo-video/clips/keyboard-navigation/keyboard-navigation.mp4), [WebM](https://github.com/gsemet/markdown-okf-schema-studio/raw/f9dc2c630b852635e8bffcd0b00b42cc886b293c/docs/demo-video/clips/keyboard-navigation/keyboard-navigation.webm)). ![Arrow keys walk into an admonition down to a nested list item, and Enter opens that line alone](https://github.com/gsemet/markdown-okf-schema-studio/raw/f9dc2c630b852635e8bffcd0b00b42cc886b293c/docs/demo-video/clips/keyboard-navigation/keyboard-navigation.gif) ## Blast radius Grade: 2. It changes which block the most common editing gesture opens, the renderer's line mapping inside boxes and the shared block move planner; a plain `git revert` restores the previous behaviour, with no data or settings change. ## Autonomous decisions - A neighbour that is not a direct block of the body (a `{table}` directive) also stops the move chord: moving past it would not keep its wrapper whole. - A move between blocks under different quote prefixes is refused with the existing "out of date" refusal; no new message. - Inside a box, a directive that shares no block of its own opens as a whole directive, and text on an opening line opens its directive, so that the lines a block of a box opens on hold no fence line of a directive around it. - Where an element's own lines cannot be told, the enclosing block or box opens, rather than a narrower range that could be wrong. - The chord's heading refusal covers every untitled admonition fence (colon, backtick, tilde) and callouts, and its `---` refusal every kind of box, because they all misrender the same way. A heading in a titled admonition, a dropdown or an alert, and a `***` line, still move. For a `{div}`, refusing too much was chosen over missing a way to write its callout class. - The palette overlap found by the new visual scenarios is fixed here, with a new requirement scenario. - The real VS Code replay of the alert lazy line opens the alert from its title, so its assertions stay. - The clip was filmed and rendered before the maintainer reviewed its storyboard: the review of `clip.md` and of the cut is pending, on this pull request. ## Known gaps The clip and its checks: - Not yet approved: the maintainer's review of the clip's storyboard and of the clip itself. - In the clip, after the save the selection is on the whole admonition, not on the saved sub-item. - The clip's contact sheet shows neither the selection of the list nor that of the sub-list; only its named frames do. - The real VS Code replay edited here runs only on the main branch or a heavy CI run. Elements of a box that do not open on their own (emptying the editor that opens erases all it holds): - The block or the box around them opens for: a formula written right under text, a quote or a `+++` line, under the text of a list item, in a table cell, after other text of its paragraph, or followed by more text in a list item or a longer paragraph; inline HTML in a definition of several lines; the summary or a table of an unpaired `
`, the summary of a `
` nested in another, a table or text written right under a closing HTML tag, and a list item whose HTML element closes outside its list. - A later paragraph of a list item whose first source line is not known (text after a code block or a directive of a tight item) opens its item. - In a directive that starts with a `---` block of options and has a later `---` line, no block of the body opens on its own: the box opens. - A paragraph holding one plain image, or an `{image}` directive, opens the box, and the move chord cannot cross it: such a move is refused, with the message about a comment or a link definition between the two blocks. - A `{table}` caption opens the admonition around it (as before this change), and a tab panel its tab item. - A paragraph holding only one tag of an HTML element (`One` then `Two`, or `Para
`) opens the whole box (as before this change). - When a `:::` admonition is left open at the end of the file and ends on a quoted one (`> :::{tip}` up to `> :::`), the title and frame of that quoted tip open the whole outer admonition, so emptying that editor removes all of it (before this change the tip's title opened the tip alone). Opening or emptying a block that takes more than itself, or leaves the box worse: - Clicking the first paragraph of a tight list item followed by hidden content or content that is no block of its own (an HTML comment, HTML, a footnote or link definition, a target, a `%` comment) opens that content with it, so emptying the editor removes it too. - Enter on the first paragraph of a list item that holds more (code, another paragraph, a directive) opens it with the item's marker; emptying it removes the marker, so the rest leaves the list item, still indented (no fence line is cut). - A `$$` line written right under a table is read as one of its rows: it opens that line, and emptying it removes the row. - A raw `
title: feat(editor): edit the pointed block inside admonitions and alerts
